dialogue.text: (low) Lantern to me. Both hands on the grip. Don't fire till I say.
Slow. Breathe out when you squeeze, not before. I've got the aim.
You don't have to do this. Tell me now if you can't.
(low) You know these dogs. Do you know which one would lie at a door like that?
If it comes through that door, it comes fast. Stay at my side, whatever happens.

options.label: Listen toward the left wall
options.detail: Wisdom (Perception); takes your action; a round ago something heavy came along the outside of the left wall and stopped close, near where you were at the hatch; you have heard nothing from it since; you cannot see through the planks

options.label: Listen back toward the hatch and the grass beyond
options.detail: Wisdom (Perception); takes your action; the hatch is 30 ft behind you at the edge of the lantern light; the two you hit went out into the grass past it

options.label: Ask Wick something
options.detail: speech is free; a longer exchange takes your action; he stands close at your left side, his lantern up in his left hand, your blaster in his right under your left hand

options.label: Read Wick through the Force
options.detail: Wisdom (Insight), takes your action; he is at your left side

options.label: Ask Wick for the blaster back
options.detail: it is in his right hand, your left hand over it holding the aim; whether he lets go is up to him

options.label: Look and listen around the floor
options.detail: Wisdom (Perception); takes your action; you stand in the dark half, in Wick's lantern light only; the strips' light begins 30 ft ahead of you, up the floor

options.label: Move a small loose thing with the Force
options.detail: Jedi Fundamentals: takes your action; one thing in sight, unattended and at rest, 10 lb or less, within 30 ft; no Force Points; not a creature, nothing held or worn, never a thing in the air; your lamp is 90 ft off, out of reach

options.label: Open the comm channel again
options.detail: the comm at your collar is closed; opened on the general hailing channel, everything you say aloud goes out over it; it is short-range

objects.label: Let go of the blaster
objects.detail: take your left hand off it; Wick keeps it in his right hand; the aim is then his alone

objects.label: Clip the hilt to your left hip
objects.detail: its home; frees your right hand; your object interaction is spent, so this turn it takes your action

objects.label: Ignite the indigo lightsaber
objects.detail: the hilt is in your right hand; the blade lights where you point it; your object interaction is spent, so this turn it takes your action

objects.label: Pick up the rake
objects.detail: on the walkway boards about 20 ft behind you, where you dropped it; you would have to go back to it; a long two-handed tool: your right hand holds the hilt

objects.label: Wick puts the lantern into your free hand
objects.detail: his to do; you need one free hand to receive it

objects.label: Take the lantern from Wick
objects.detail: you take it from his hand yourself: an object interaction

objects.label: Wick takes the blaster's grip in both hands

movement.label: Stay where you are, on the walkway
Go on up the walkway about 30 ft, to where the strips' light begins
Go back about 20 ft to the rake
Go back down the walkway to the hatch (~30 ft)

visible.label: Wick, close at your left side, in PELL's coveralls and gloves; his open lantern up in his left hand; your blaster in his right, your left hand over it, the muzzle held up the walkway at the foot of the small door. He let you guide it without a word and breathed with you. He has not fired.

The far-end hatch, about 30 ft behind you at the far edge of the lantern light: shut and bolted from inside, the bolt home. Three cuts burned through its planks low along the sill, all dark; you pressed the ember out.

Out past the hatch, in the long grass, 30 ft and more behind you: the two you hit went straight out from the hatch into the dark; you could not hear where either stopped. From out there your own voice said 'I heard you come round. Take your time.', and earlier something said 'Mum?' in Wick's voice. This round: nothing.

Beyond the left wall: a round ago something heavy came low through the grass along the outside of the wall and stopped close, near where you were at the hatch, only the planks between. You came up the floor past that stretch of wall. You have heard nothing from it since. You cannot tell where it is now.

Beyond the end wall, to the left of the hatch, 30 ft and more behind you: earlier something heavy came round the corner and settled out there. You have heard nothing move there since. You cannot see it.
The grain rake, where you dropped it on the walkway boards about 20 ft behind you, at the edge of Wick's lantern light

The line of boot prints in the grain dust, running down the whole floor from the spill at her lantern to the sill of the hatch behind you and stopping there, nothing coming back; an even walking stride; a small work boot, a woman's size, a ridged farm-boot sole.

The board walkway running the length of the floor: you tested it end to end with the rake: every board knocks dead and solid on its spikes and sleepers; no space under it. Here in the dark half only Wick's lantern lights it; the strips' white light begins 30 ft ahead of you.

Rows of low slatted drying beds either side of the walkway, grain spread level in them, undisturbed; each a slatted tray over a shallow closed air box, a hand deep, fed by a sheet-metal duct from the right-hand wall; nothing bigger than a rat could get in

The wide double cart door in the left wall, 50 ft up the floor ahead of you: two plank leaves on iron strap hinges, shut, an iron ring pull on each; the heavy squared timber bar across both leaves, home in both iron brackets. Barred from inside.

70 ft up the walkway, in the white light: her hooded lantern with the blue tape on its handle, upright on the boards, out and cold, burned dry where it stands; beside it the bed raked level in even strokes to about halfway, rough past that, grain spilled onto the walkway.
The small door in the end wall, 90 ft up the floor, shut and latched from inside: the hook in its eye. Your lamp lies lit at its foot. One of them lies against the other side of it.
Outside the small door, 90 ft up the floor: one of them, lying against the door at its foot, unseen. You have heard nothing from it since it lay down.

Your lamp, lit, on its side on the boards at the foot of the small door, 90 ft up the floor; its light a small patch on the boards far off. Whatever lies outside that door is a foot from it, on the other side of the planks.
The switch box on the frame by the small door, 90 ft up the floor, its switch thrown; the strips lit over the near half of the floor
The fan housing and sheet-metal ducts along the right-hand wall, silent; branch ducts run in under each bed

notes: Combat, round 9, still your turn. Initiative: you 21, the drover-dogs 7. When your turn ends, theirs comes.

Left this turn: your action, your bonus action, your movement (30 ft) and your reaction. Your object interaction is spent (you took hold of the blaster); handling another object this turn takes your action. Speech is free.

Your left hand is over the blaster in Wick's right hand, holding the aim on the foot of the small door, 90 ft up the walkway. Your right hand holds the unlit hilt. To take the lantern, one hand has to come free.
The small door is shut, its hook in its eye. What lies against it is on the far side of the planks, unseen; you aimed where something lying at its foot would be.
Wick has never fired a blaster. You told him not to fire unless you are threatened; you have not told him to fire.

You stand on the walkway about 90 ft in from the small door, about 30 ft up from the hatch, in the dark half, in Wick's lantern light only (about 30 ft); the strips' white light begins 30 ft ahead of you.
A round ago something heavy stopped close outside the left wall near the hatch end. Since then you have heard nothing from it, or from anything else. You cannot tell whether it moved.
The voices outside repeat words they have heard, word for word, in the voice that said them: yours, and Wick's.
The two you hit went out into the long grass past the hatch. Earlier something settled beyond the end wall left of the hatch; you have heard nothing there since.
The cart door, 50 ft ahead in the left wall, is barred. The hatch behind you is bolted. Your holster is empty.
The voice down the rise calls every few minutes; it last called just before your round-2 turn.
In your robe pockets: the folding knife (folded), the flat cell, three pairs of work gloves. In your backpack: the canteen, the dead datapad, eight rations. The comm at your collar is closed.
It is just over three hours since the sun went down. It will not be light for about twelve hours.

left.label: on the blaster in Wick's hand, holding the aim

plan_result.reason: Wick is at your side, the blaster's muzzle held up the walkway at the foot of the small door by your left hand over his, and he is breathing with you. To take the lantern you need a free hand: your left is on the blaster, holding the aim, and your right holds the hilt. Which hand takes it is yours to say. It is still your turn: your action, bonus action, 30 ft of movement and your reaction remain; your object interaction is spent.

position_label: standing on the walkway about 90 ft in from the small end door, about 30 ft up from the far-end hatch, in the dark half; the unlit hilt in your right hand; your left hand over the blaster in Wick's right hand, holding the aim on the foot of the small door; Wick close at your left side, his lantern up in his left hand; the rake on the boards about 20 ft behind you

pending_steps.text: Tell him to put his other hand on the grip, preparing him to fire the blaster at the dog on the other side of the door

pending_reason: To take the lantern you need a free hand: your left is on the blaster holding the aim, your right holds the hilt. Taking it and telling Wick to put his other hand on the grip run only if you submit them again, with the hand you choose.
